fix(scores): qualify functionOptionColumns so ?include=functionoption is not ambiguous (#605)

Fixes a prod outage introduced by #594, merged earlier today. Every
questionnaire and every question-level breakdown is returning 500 until
this deploys.

`GET /api/v1/scores?...&include=functionoption` fails with `column
reference "functionid" is ambiguous` (42702). `trapError` has no 42702
case, so it falls through to a bare 500 `{"data":null,"error":"server
error"}` — no field, no constraint name, nothing the frontend or an
operator can act on.

No Go code had to change for this to break. Migration `0060` added a
`functionid` column to `scores`, and `functionOptionColumns` has listed
`functionid` unqualified since it was written:

```go
functionOptionColumns = []string{"functionoptions.functionoptionid", "functionid", "score", "optionname", "description"}
```

That was safe for as long as only `functionoptions` had a `functionid`.
`FindScores` is the single place the list is selected across a join to
`scores`, and 0060 put a second `functionid` on the other side of that
join. The schema moved underneath a query that nobody edited.

## The fix

The list is now fully table-qualified, and the write path gets its own
unqualified copy. Both are needed: a bare name is ambiguous in the join,
and an INSERT column list and `RETURNING` both reject a table-qualified
name. `Save` builds `RETURNING` from the write list rather than
repeating the names in a string literal, so the two orders cannot drift
— the old comment at that line was already apologizing for the
duplication the split now removes.

Qualifying `score`, `optionname` and `description` alongside
`functionid` is not tidiness. `functionid` is simply the collision that
happened to land first; `score` is the next one in line the moment any
future join puts a table carrying that name opposite `functionoptions`,
and the failure mode is identical — a correct-looking query that worked
in CI against a schema that no longer matches prod.

The list's two other consumers, `FindFunctionOptions` and
`FindFunctionOptionByID`, select from `functionoptions` alone. They are
unaffected either way, and the qualified names are still valid there.

## Blast radius

`FindScores` is the only broken site. Every other query that joins
`scores` to `functionoptions` aliases the table — the pillar aggregate's
`answers` CTE, `copyPreviousScores`, `scorediff`, the `FindAnswers`
subquery — so all of them were already immune. `functionid` is the only
column name the two tables share apart from `functionoptionid`, which
was already qualified.

That is also why the breakage looked partial rather than total.
`/scores/aggregate` is a different query and kept working, so the
dashboard tiles and the radar chart rendered normal numbers while the
question-level breakdown underneath them reported "0 questions".
Scoring, rollover and the data-call export are all unaffected, and no
write path was ever broken.

Nothing is wrong with the data. The schema is correct and the migrations
applied cleanly; only the query was wrong. Deploying this is the whole
remediation — no cleanup, no backfill.

## Why CI did not catch it

`?include=functionoption` had no end-to-end coverage. The whole include
branch was untested, which is how a query that cannot parse reached prod
with a green suite on #594. The Emberfall case added here closes that.

Worth noting the general shape, because the next migration that
denormalizes a column will hit it the same way: a column added to one
table can break a query against another, and nothing in the toolchain
connects those two facts. The Go code compiles, the migration tests
pass, the model tests pass. Only an end-to-end request against the
migrated schema fails, so coverage of the read paths is the only thing
that catches this class at all.

## Testing

- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration` and `make test-e2e` green
(263 cases).
- The new Emberfall case was verified by mutating the fix away rather
than by passing once: reverting the single qualified name back to
`"functionid"` and re-running produces exactly one failure, the new
case.
- The statement itself was reproduced and cleared at the SQL level
against the test database — 42702 before, parses and returns rows after.
- No OpenAPI change; `make generate-openapi` produces no diff.

fix(#491): enforce one answer per system per question per data call (#594)

Closes #491. Fixes the create path behind the symptom tracked in
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#336. **Draft until prod and dev are confirmed
clean** — both migrations refuse to apply while duplicates exist, and a
failing migration crash-loops the deploy. See "Before this can leave
draft" below.

## Summary

A system can hold more than one stored answer to the same question in
one data call. `Save()` branches on `ScoreID == 0` to insert, with no
lookup on the natural key, so any caller that does not know the existing
`scoreid` creates a second row — and nothing in the schema prevents it.

This adds the uniqueness that should always have existed and makes the
write path agree with it.

- **Denormalizes** `functionid` onto `scores` (0060), maintained by a
trigger and pinned by a composite FK, so the natural key becomes
indexable
- **Enforces** one answer per `(fismasystemid, datacallid, functionid)`
(0061)
- **Resolves** the natural key on create, so a caller without the
existing `scoreid` updates instead of inserting, with a single 23505
retry for the concurrent case
- **Rejects** an update carrying an option from a different question,
rather than silently writing the natural-key row
- **Does not** repair existing rows — that reconciliation is manual, see
below

Note the natural key is the **question**, not the selected option. Two
rows holding different `functionoptions` of one `function` are the
common duplicate shape, and they differ on `functionoptionid`, so
nothing keyed on the answer would catch them.

A concrete thing this fixes: `QuestionnairePage.tsx` in ztmf-ui carries
the comment *"a second Complete would POST a duplicate row and
double-weight the question in the pillar average"*, and works around it
by re-seeding the saved state after every Complete. That second POST now
resolves onto the existing answer, so the workaround becomes defence in
depth rather than the only thing standing between a double-click and a
skewed pillar score.

## Why `functionid` has to move onto the row

An answer's question is reachable only as `scores.functionoptionid ->
functionoptions.functionid`. Postgres cannot index across that hop, so
the natural key is not expressible as the schema stands — that is the
whole of why #491 needs a schema change rather than a query fix.

Two mechanisms keep the copy honest, and they cover different failure
modes:

- `trg_scores_set_functionid` derives `functionid` on every write to
`scores`, so no writer — app, seed, psql, a future importer — can set it
to anything else. It cannot see writes to the parent table.
- `scores_functionoption_function_fkey` covers exactly that gap. The
questionnaire catalogue is edited by hand out of band; repointing a
`functionoption` at a different `function` would stale every referencing
score behind the trigger's back. `NO ACTION` blocks it.

Neither is redundant, and **neither is the load-bearing guarantee**:
`session_replication_role = 'replica'` disables triggers *and* FK checks
together, which is precisely how the orphaned rows described below got
in despite an existing FK. A unique index is still enforced in replica
mode. The index is the protection; the trigger and FK are correctness
aids for ordinary writes.

`NOT NULL` on the new column is not tidiness either — a btree unique
index treats NULLs as distinct, so one NULL `functionid` would let 0061
build cleanly and enforce nothing for that row. That is why the backfill
and the `SET NOT NULL` are atomic in one migration rather than split
across the 0027–0029 pattern.

## The write path

`Save()` treats create and update differently, deliberately.

**Create** resolves `(fismasystemid, datacallid, question)` and updates
the existing answer if there is one. This is the #491 fix itself.

**Update** rejects an option belonging to a *different* question with a
400. A score's question is part of its identity, so that request is
malformed rather than an instruction to write elsewhere. Resolving the
natural key there would silently modify a row the caller never named and
hand back a `scoreid` it never asked for, leaving a buggy client
believing it had edited the row it addressed. Worth knowing what `main`
does with the same request: it rewrites the row's question, which both
collides with that question's existing answer and discards the answer
this row was holding — so this is one of the ways the defect is
manufactured today. The questionnaire always PUTs the row for the
question on screen, so it never trips the check.

The 23505 retry is gated on the natural key actually resolving, not on
the error alone: `trapError` collapses every 23505 into `ErrNotUnique`
and discards the `PgError`, so the constraint name is not recoverable
here and a future second unique index on `scores` would otherwise be
retried as if it were this one.

`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` was considered for the create path
and rejected, in order of severity:

1. It bypasses `scoreUpdateIsNoOp`, which is the whole of #412/#413 —
the questionnaire PUTs on every Next click and that guard stops a
read-through restamping the editor. Once a POST can resolve onto an
existing row, a repeated POST *is* a read-through, so `ON CONFLICT`
reintroduces the regression on the create path.
2. It cannot express `notes_is_ai_summary`'s only-set-when-non-nil
semantics without conditional SQL, at which point the single-statement
advantage is gone.
3. `recordEvent` derives the action from the squirrel builder's Go type,
so an `InsertBuilder` that updated would log `created`. Harmless for
progress (both actions are in the allowlist), wrong for the Events page
and `docs/timespent_queries.sql`.

The lookup is skipped when the caller preloaded the row and the option
is unchanged — the stored row is then the natural-key row by
construction, so the hot PUT path pays nothing.

`SaveScore` now takes `scoreid` only from the URL path. A POST body
carrying one used to survive the bind and route the request into the
update branch, where it authorized and wrote against the *stored* row's
system while silently ignoring the body's `fismasystemid`. Not a
security hole — the authorization was on the stored row, correctly — but
it gave POST two meanings.

A POST that resolves onto an existing answer still returns **201** with
the canonical row: `respond` keys status off `r.Method`, the body
carries the real `scoreid`, and returning 200 would break any client
keyed on 201.

## Existing duplicates are not repaired here

Where a duplicated pair holds two genuinely different answers, only the
data owner can say which is right, so the repair is manual and happens
before this merges. Both migrations therefore open with a guard:

| Migration | Token | Blocks on |
|---|---|---|
| 0060 | `ZTMF491_ORPHANED_SCORES` | `scores` rows whose
`functionoptionid` resolves to nothing |
| 0061 | `ZTMF491_DUPLICATE_ANSWERS` | duplicate `(system, data call,
question)` groups |

Without them a premature deploy fails on a bare 23502/23505 from inside
a crash-looping task, which says nothing about what to do. Both messages
are countable and greppable, matching the `MIGRATION_VERSION_MISMATCH`
treatment in `migrations.go`.

The orphaned rows deserve a note: they are already invisible to the
application (every read path inner-joins `functionoptions` and drops
them), because they name a `functionoptionid` that resolves to nothing.
What is unrecoverable is the *question* — nothing on `scores` records
which question a row answers, so such a row cannot be re-attached
programmatically, and any notes it carries have to be exported for
review rather than assumed disposable. Counts per environment are on the
internal tracking issue, not here.

## Scale

Duplicate counts, affected cycles and the per-environment census live on
the internal tracking issue (CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#336) rather than
in this public repo. What matters for reviewing the code: the defect is
present in more than one closed cycle, the shapes are a mix of
same-answer pairs and pairs that genuinely disagree, and whether any
*open* cycle is affected is the one census result that would change this
approach — a duplicate there is an answer someone may be editing, and it
needs a person rather than a rule.

## What stays, and why

**The `DISTINCT ON` in `copyPreviousScores` stays.** Removing it is the
tempting call and it is wrong: that copy is a single `INSERT ...
SELECT`, so under the new index a duplicated source cycle does not copy
a duplicate — it aborts with 23505 and the entire annual rollover emits
nothing. That is the #411 all-or-nothing foot-gun the INNER JOINs
defuse, reopened on a different error class, and it is reachable from a
restore of a pre-cleanup backup.

**The pillar `answers` CTE gets no `DISTINCT`.** With the index holding,
at most one row exists per `(fismasystemid, datacallid, functionid)`, so
the fan-out that double-weights a question cannot occur. A `DISTINCT ON`
there would mask a lost index by producing plausible numbers instead of
a visibly wrong average; a comment now says so, naming 0061.

`scorediff`'s `FULL OUTER JOIN` cartesian across duplicate pairs also
stops being reachable once the data is clean.

## Testing

`make test-unit` and `make test-integration` green. Each new assertion
was verified by mutating the production code, not by passing once:

- **The write path** — disabling the natural-key resolve fails all four
`Save` tests. The concurrency one fails with three real `not unique`
errors, which is the retry earning its place rather than a hypothetical.
- **The migration guards** — `scoresdataguards_integration_test.go` runs
each migration's real SQL from the registry against data it dirties
itself, inside a rolled-back transaction. The orphan case manufactures
its fixture under `session_replication_role = 'replica'`, the same
mechanism that created the real ones. Both the refusal *and* the
clean-apply are asserted, so a guard that always threw would not pass.
- **The DB layer directly** — the index rejects a second option of the
same question; the trigger derives, self-corrects a supplied
`functionid`, and follows an option change; an unknown
`functionoptionid` raises **23503, not 23502**, which is what keeps it a
400 rather than a 500 (`trapError` has no 23502 case, and NOT NULL is
evaluated before the AFTER-trigger FK).

The three rollover dedup tests now suspend the index around their
fixture, reading the DDL back from `pg_indexes` so the restore cannot
drift. They are kept rather than retired: this PR does not clean the
data, so a duplicated source cycle stays a real state. `-p 1` on
`test-integration` is required by that — packages currently run in
parallel against one database and the index drop is global.

## Coordination outside this repo: the Snowflake sync

**`ztmf-insights` replicates `scores` to Snowflake with `SELECT *`, so
`0060`'s new column propagates to it.**

- `backend/cmd/data-sync/internal/sync/sync.go:186` registers `scores`
for replication (read-only against our database; it performs no writes)
- `backend/internal/export/postgres.go:143` builds the extract as
`SELECT * FROM <table>` and takes the column names from
`rows.FieldDescriptions()`
- `backend/internal/export/snowflake.go:289` then emits `INSERT INTO
<table> (<those same columns>) VALUES ...`

The column list is therefore ours, handed straight to Snowflake. There
is no `CREATE TABLE` or `ALTER TABLE` anywhere in that repo, so the
Snowflake schema is managed externally and will not pick the column up
on its own. The expected failure is `invalid identifier 'FUNCTIONID'`
and a failed `scores` table on the next sync run.

**Neither repo's CI would catch this** — different repo, different
deploy, and the job runs on a schedule. `FUNCTIONID` needs adding to the
Snowflake `scores` table before this merges.

The reporting queries in `ztmf-insights/reporting/queries.py` are
unaffected: they read `events` filtered on `action IN
('created','updated')`, and both members stay in the set.

## Before this can leave draft

The same cleanup is needed wherever the new image starts, not just prod:

| Database | Deploys | Clean by |
|---|---|---|
| prod | on merge | before merging |
| dev | from the PR, once out of draft | **before taking this out of
draft** |
| impl | on the nightly sync merge | ~a day after merge |

Per-PR environments use their own seeded throwaway database and need
nothing.

Both of these must return zero in an environment before the image starts
there:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM public.scores s
  LEFT JOIN public.functionoptions fo ON fo.functionoptionid = s.functionoptionid
 WHERE fo.functionoptionid IS NULL;

SELECT count(*) FROM (
  SELECT 1 FROM public.scores s
    JOIN public.functionoptions fo ON fo.functionoptionid = s.functionoptionid
   GROUP BY s.fismasystemid, s.datacallid, fo.functionid
  HAVING count(*) > 1) d;
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A write for an existing system/question/data call updates the
existing row rather than inserting a second, regardless of whether the
caller supplies an id
- [x] Uniqueness is enforced at the database layer on system + question
+ data call
- [x] Rollover cannot introduce or propagate duplicates — satisfied by
#590 and now structural
- [ ] Existing duplicates are reconciled — tracked on
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#336 and performed before merge, **not**
deferred past it: the constraint cannot apply until it is done
- [x] Regression coverage for the create path and for rollover

## Notes for reviewers

- **Follow-up worth taking**: `answers.go:76` joins with
`scores.functionoptionid IN (SELECT ... WHERE
selected.functionid=functions.functionid)`. Migration `0055` exists
specifically because that subquery was a 47.7s Join Filter. With
`scores.functionid` present it collapses to a plain `scores.functionid =
functions.functionid` equality that the new index serves directly.
Deliberately **not** done here — the export is correctness-sensitive and
deserves its own PR with its own measurement.
- **Emberfall fixtures now share a row.** `functionoptions` 1-4 are all
options of one question (7001), and the suite POSTs five of them for
system 1001 / data call 5 — so it has been manufacturing the very
duplicates this fixes. All 230 still pass, because each POST returns the
row reflecting its own values. Nothing asserts across those fixtures
today, but a test added between them could fail confusingly.

- **Historical pillar scores will change** for affected systems when the
cleanup runs — they stop being double-weighted. That is the fix, but it
is a visible change to published numbers, and it happens at cleanup time
rather than at deploy time.
- **Rolling-deploy window**: between 0061 committing and the old task
draining, an old-code POST creating a second answer gets a 400 instead
of a 201.
- **Questionnaire versioning**: the key assumes a data call pins one
questionnaire version, which holds whether versioning mints new
`functionid`s or reuses them with a version column. If a cycle ever
spans versions, the version column joins the index. The composite FK
will also block any versioning work that edits `functionoptions` in
place — by design, since versioning should add rows rather than mutate
them.
- `_test_data_empire.sql`'s `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` clauses have no
conflict target, so they will now silently swallow natural-key conflicts
too. Harmless today (the seed is duplicate-free and orphan-free,
verified), but worth knowing if a future seed edit introduces one.

feat(misc#376): CloudFront standard logs and ALB connection logs for TLS telemetry (#602)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#376 · Part of
[ztmf#572](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/issues/572)

## Summary

Turns on TLS telemetry for the PQC work: CloudFront standard logs (v2)
and ALB connection logs. Both write to the existing `ztmf-logs` bucket
and expire after 90 days.

## Changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `terraform.tf` | AWS provider `~> 5.82.2` → `~> 5.89.0` |
| `cloudfront.tf` | v2 log delivery (source, S3 destination, delivery) →
`cloudfront/<env>/{yyyy}/{MM}/{dd}/`, JSON |
| `alb-internal.tf` | `connection_logs` → `rest-api-alb-conn/` |
| `s3.tf` | Bucket policy: `rest-api-alb-conn/*` for ELB, `cloudfront/*`
for `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`. New lifecycle config: both prefixes
expire at 90 days |

## Decisions

- **Provider bump:** the v2 delivery resources arrived in 5.83.0, and
5.89.0 fixes a `suffix_path` bug. Changelog 5.83–5.89 is additive for
every resource type we use.
- **v2 instead of legacy `logging_config`:** legacy logging needs ACLs
enabled on the bucket.
- **Explicit field list:** leaves out `cs(Cookie)` and `cs-uri-query`,
so session cookies never reach the logs. Keeps `c-ip` and
`cs(User-Agent)`, which are needed to identify the remaining TLS 1.2
clients (pqc 5,
[ztmf-misc#379](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/379)).
- **Names carry `name_suffix`:** delivery names are account-scoped, and
dev and impl share an account.
- **`pr-env` pin unchanged:** that root needs none of these resources.

## Rollout

- **Draft = no apply.** Marking ready triggers the dev apply
(`orchestration-dev`).
- **Dev:** wait about 4h, then confirm objects under `cloudfront/dev/`
and `rest-api-alb-conn/`.
- **Merge = prod apply.** Impl follows on the nightly sync.

## Check before marking ready

- [x] No lifecycle rules set outside Terraform on
`ztmf-logs-<acct>-use1` (dev and prod). The new resource owns the
bucket's whole lifecycle config and would replace them. Checked
2026-09-30: neither bucket has a lifecycle configuration.
- [x] `terraform plan` on dev shows only the intended adds and changes,
and nothing unrelated from the provider bump. Checked 2026-09-30: 4 to
add (three log delivery resources, the lifecycle config), 2 to change
(`connection_logs` on the ALB, the bucket policy), 0 to destroy.

## Verified

- `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass on 5.89.0.
- The connection-log regex below parses the documented 12-field sample,
the current 15-field format, and failed handshakes.

## Not verified

- No plan against prod state.
- Log delivery itself, until the dev apply.

## Note for pqc 3
([ztmf-misc#377](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/377))
and pqc 6
([ztmf-misc#380](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/380))

ALB connection logs describe only the client side of the listener, not
the hop from the ALB to the targets. In dev the client negotiates TLS
1.3 with a classical key exchange (`secp256r1` in a 2026-10-01 sample),
so once pqc 3 moves the listener to the post-quantum policy, these logs
should show whether that hop switches to a hybrid group.

<details><summary>Athena: CloudFront TLS version share</summary>

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE cloudfront_v2 (
  `date` string, `time` string, c_ip string, cs_user_agent string,
  ssl_protocol string, ssl_cipher string, time_to_first_byte string,
  sc_status string, cs_uri_stem string)
PARTITIONED BY (day string)
ROW FORMAT SERDE 'org.openx.data.jsonserde.JsonSerDe'
WITH SERDEPROPERTIES (
  'mapping.c_ip'='c-ip', 'mapping.cs_user_agent'='cs(User-Agent)',
  'mapping.ssl_protocol'='ssl-protocol', 'mapping.ssl_cipher'='ssl-cipher',
  'mapping.time_to_first_byte'='time-to-first-byte',
  'mapping.sc_status'='sc-status', 'mapping.cs_uri_stem'='cs-uri-stem')
LOCATION 's3://ztmf-logs-<acct>-use1/cloudfront/prod/'
TBLPROPERTIES (
  'projection.enabled'='true',
  'projection.day.type'='date', 'projection.day.format'='yyyy/MM/dd',
  'projection.day.range'='2026/10/01,NOW',
  'projection.day.interval'='1', 'projection.day.interval.unit'='DAYS',
  'storage.location.template'='s3://ztmf-logs-<acct>-use1/cloudfront/prod/${day}/');

-- TLS version share
SELECT ssl_protocol, count(*) AS requests,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct
FROM cloudfront_v2 WHERE day >= '2026/10/01'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- Who is still on TLS 1.2 (pqc 5)
SELECT url_decode(cs_user_agent) AS ua, c_ip, count(*) AS requests
FROM cloudfront_v2 WHERE ssl_protocol = 'TLSv1.2'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 50;
```
</details>

<details><summary>Athena: ALB connection key exchange and handshake
latency</summary>

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE alb_conn (
  `timestamp` string, client_ip string, client_port int, listener_port int,
  tls_protocol string, tls_cipher string, tls_handshake_latency string,
  leaf_client_cert_subject string, leaf_client_cert_validity string,
  leaf_client_cert_serial_number string, tls_verify_status string,
  conn_trace_id string, tls_keyexchange string, elb string, ip_address string)
PARTITIONED BY (day string)
ROW FORMAT SERDE 'org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.RegexSerDe'
WITH SERDEPROPERTIES ('input.regex' =
  '^([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ([0-9]*) ([0-9]*) ([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ("[^"]*"|[^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ([^ ]*) ?([^ ]*) ?([^ ]*) ?([^ ]*).*$')
LOCATION 's3://ztmf-logs-<acct>-use1/rest-api-alb-conn/AWSLogs/<acct>/elasticloadbalancing/us-east-1/'
TBLPROPERTIES (
  'projection.enabled'='true',
  'projection.day.type'='date', 'projection.day.format'='yyyy/MM/dd',
  'projection.day.range'='2026/10/01,NOW',
  'projection.day.interval'='1', 'projection.day.interval.unit'='DAYS',
  'storage.location.template'='s3://ztmf-logs-<acct>-use1/rest-api-alb-conn/AWSLogs/<acct>/elasticloadbalancing/us-east-1/${day}/');

SELECT tls_protocol, tls_keyexchange, count(*) AS connections,
       approx_percentile(CAST(tls_handshake_latency AS double), 0.5)  AS p50_s,
       approx_percentile(CAST(tls_handshake_latency AS double), 0.95) AS p95_s
FROM alb_conn
WHERE day >= '2026/10/01' AND tls_handshake_latency <> '-'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
```
</details>

feat(misc#344): nightly pr-env reaper and fleet alarm (#601)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#344

Part of the ephemeral PR environments epic
(CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#321). Teardown on PR close is the primary
cleanup; this adds the backstop and the backstop for the backstop.

`scripts/pr-env-reaper.sh` runs nightly at 07:00 UTC from the new
pr-env-reaper.yml and covers both repos. For each `pr/<repo>/<n>` state
key it destroys the environment if the PR is closed, or if the PR has
had no deploy for 7 days, in which case it also comments on the PR that
the next push rebuilds it. It removes the state object and the PR's
images and retires the `pr-<repo>-<n>` GitHub Environment. It then
retires any `pr-*` environment in either repo whose PR is closed, and
reports what it cannot fix: a destroy that failed twice, a `pr-*` ECS
service with no state key, and an open PR's state key with no running
service. Any finding, or a failed run, comments on one tracking issue in
ztmf-misc, or opens it if none is open. The script runs by hand with
`--dry-run`, and the workflow can be dispatched with `dry_run` or
`force_failure`.

`infrastructure/monitoring-pr-env.tf` adds the layer that does not
depend on GitHub: a CloudWatch alarm on a Metrics Insights query summing
RunningTaskCount across the cluster's services other than ztmf-api. It
pages the existing ztmf-alarms topic when more than
`pr_env_max_environments` (10) tasks run for 10 minutes.

Divergence from the ticket: there is no AWS Budgets alert. Budgets can
only filter on activated cost-allocation tags, and activation is
payer-account only; this account gets "Linked account doesn't have
access to cost allocation tags". The alarm covers the runaway-fleet case
the budget was for.

New repo secret PR_ENV_REAPER_TOKEN: a fine-grained PAT on ztmf,
ztmf-ui, and ztmf-misc (Administration, Deployments, Issues, and Pull
requests read/write), since GITHUB_TOKEN cannot comment on ztmf-ui PRs,
delete its environments, or file issues in ztmf-misc. It stands in for
the misc#196 service account.

Verified: a dry run against dev kept the one live environment
(ztmf-ui#744) with no findings; with TTL 0 it walked the full reap path
for that environment without changing anything. The alarm's query
returns the expected 1.0 against dev. actionlint, shellcheck, `terraform
fmt`, and `terraform validate` are clean, and the backend unit,
integration, and e2e suites pass. A scheduled workflow can only be
dispatched once it is on main, so after merge I will dispatch it with
dry_run, with force_failure to confirm the tracking issue, and for real,
and record the results on misc#344.

commits.message:
fix(misc#398): close three content-write gaps in the questionnaire catalog API (#599)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#398.

Three defects in the content-write endpoints ztmf#129 shipped without a
UI, carved out of ztmf-misc#396. No migration, no schema change, no
frontend.

## Why

**An OpDiv admin could rewrite the HHS-wide catalog.**
`SaveQuestion`/`SaveFunction` gated on `IsAdmin()`, which includes
`OPDIV_ADMIN`. The catalog is one mutable set, so an OpDiv admin editing
a question changes what every other OpDiv is scored on.
`CanWriteHHSWide()` has existed since #467 for exactly this and had one
call site. No UI reaches these endpoints, so it takes a deliberate API
call.

**`Question.validate()` was a commented-out stub** and `Save` called
nothing, so an empty POST inserted empty text and `pillarid` 0 — failing
later on the FK, naming no field.

**`functionoptions` had no write path**, though its rows are the 1-4
scoring scale every answer points at.

## What

- `IsAdmin()` → `CanWriteHHSWide()` on `SaveQuestion`, `SaveFunction`,
and the new `SaveFunctionOption`.
- `Question.validate()` mirrors `Function.validate()`: `question`,
`notesprompt`, `pillarid` required. All three are `NOT NULL` and the
UPDATE branch sets each unconditionally, so a partial PUT was a silent
clobber rather than a partial write. Text fields are checked with
`TrimSpace` — whitespace-only satisfies `NOT NULL` but renders blank in
the questionnaire and the export. `order` stays optional — a `*int`, so
omitting it preserves the stored rank.
- `FunctionOption` gains `validate`, `Save` and `FindFunctionOptionByID`
behind `POST /functions/{functionid}/options` and `PUT
/functionoptions/{functionoptionid}`. Create is nested so the owner
comes from the path; update is flat because an option's function is a
fact about the stored row. `score` bounded 1-4,
`optionname`/`description` to their varchars — `trapError` doesn't map
22001, so unbounded they surface as 500s. `optionname` is `TrimSpace`d
for emptiness but length-checked raw, since the raw string is what gets
stored.
- **Ids are re-pinned from the route after decoding, on all three Save
handlers.** `getJSON` decodes any field on the struct, so a POST
carrying its own id landed in the id and sent `Save` down its UPDATE
branch — silently rewriting that row under a `201 Created`.
- Path ids parse via `strconv` rather than `fmt.Sscan`, whose default
verb reads `0012` as octal 10. `pathInt32` returns `(int32, bool)` and
reports `0` as unusable alongside parse failures.
- **A PUT whose path id routes but cannot address a row is a 404, not a
create.** `[0-9]+` matches both `0` and a value past `int32`; each
parsed to a bare `0`, which `SaveQuestion`/`SaveFunction` could not
distinguish from "no id in the path", so `Save` took its create branch
and inserted a row — under the PUT's own `204`, with no id returned. The
three Save handlers now 404 before any DB access; the single-resource
GETs do the same; the list endpoints keep their empty-list contract.

**Trap worth flagging:** `isValidIntID` can't be used for `pillarid`. It
takes `any` but type-switches only `int32`/`*int32`, and
`Question.PillarID` is a plain `int`, so it reports `false` for *every*
value. Explicit comparison instead, with a test pinning that valid
pillarids pass.

Pillar existence is left to the FK: 23503 already maps to
`ErrNoReference` and a 400, and `pillars.go` carries no finder to
pre-empt it with.

## Deliberately not done

**No `DELETE`.** An option nothing references yet can be deleted, and
until the catalog is versioned that is a permanent, unlogged mutation
with no draft to do it in. ztmf-misc#396 adds it and carries the
acceptance criterion.

**No four-options / no-duplicate-scores rule.** That is #396's publish
gate — enforcing it on write would make a set impossible to edit, since
this ships no delete.

**Known spec quirk:** swag can't scope `@Param` per `@Router`, so the
option paths each declare both ids. `/questions` already has this;
fixing it means splitting the handler.

## Testing

Emberfall green at **262 cases**, up from 230 on main: the `OPDIV_ADMIN`
→ 403 matrix across all six routes, the `validate()` 400s, the options
lifecycle, body-id-override creates each followed by a re-read proving
the row the body named is untouched, and `PUT .../0` and `PUT
.../99999999999` → 404 on all three routes. `make test-integration`
green, fixtures cleaned up. Unit tests touch no database — the
unusable-id 404 lands before any query, so it is covered without one.

Mutation-checked rather than assumed: reverting a gate to `IsAdmin()`
fails exactly 4 subtests, moving a gate below `getJSON` fails only the
test written for that, letting `0` back through as a valid id fails 4,
and dropping a length bound or a `TrimSpace` fails only its own cases.

`go build`, `go vet` and `staticcheck` clean; `make generate-openapi`
regenerates byte-identical.

feat(misc#342): per-PR environment workflow for ztmf PRs (#593)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#342

Adds `.github/workflows/orchestration-pr.yml`, the ztmf half of per-PR
environments (epic ztmf-misc#321). On every non-draft PR to main it
builds the API image's test target as `pr-ztmf-<n>-<sha>` into
`ztmf/api-pr`, reads `ztmf_ui_tag` from SSM for the frontend image,
applies `infrastructure/pr-env` with state keyed `pr/ztmf/<n>`, and
posts the environment URL as a single comment that is edited in place on
each push. The deploy job runs under a GitHub Environment named
`pr-ztmf-<n>` with the URL set, so the PR gets the View deployment
button and a per-push deployment history. The environment carries no
secrets; the OIDC role ARN comes from the repo-level `PR_ENV_ROLEARN`.

On close, merged or not, it destroys the root with one retry, deletes
the state object and the PR's images, marks the environment's
deployments inactive, and deletes the environment using
`PR_ENV_ADMIN_TOKEN` (skipped with a warning if that secret is absent).
A failed teardown comments the manual destroy commands on the PR so the
failure lands with the author. On merge it also builds main's test
target as `main-<sha>` into `ztmf/api-pr` and writes
`ztmf_api_test_tag`, the API image a ztmf-ui PR environment runs
(ztmf-misc#343).

Per-PR concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a close
queued behind a push wins and nothing is cancelled mid-apply. Drafts
skip build and deploy; `ready_for_review` triggers the first deploy.

Bootstrapping: ztmf-ui does not yet publish `ztmf_ui_tag` (that is the
workflow half of ztmf-misc#343), so `ui-0a1ec22` was built from ztmf-ui
main and pushed to `ztmf/ui` by hand, and `ztmf_ui_tag` set to it, on
2026-09-16. The deploy job fails with an explicit error naming that
parameter if it is ever missing.

Behavior change for reviewers: every non-draft ztmf PR now gets an
environment and a comment. Dependabot PRs are the exception: their runs
see only Dependabot secrets, which do not include PR_ENV_ROLEARN, so
build and teardown skip them. The PR-triggered dev deploy in
orchestration-dev.yml keeps running alongside until the cutover in
ztmf-misc#345.

Verification: actionlint clean. This PR exercises the workflow on
itself; the acceptance run (URL comment, View deployment, usable
environment, rebuild on push) is recorded on ztmf-misc#342. Teardown was
exercised on 2026-09-24 with a throwaway PR (#600): destroy, state
delete, image delete, deployment inactive, and environment deletion all
ran clean in
https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/actions/runs/36024017536, and no
failure comment posted. The `main-<sha>` publish runs when this merges.

chore(deps): bump axios to 1.20.0 to clear eight high-severity advisories

Snyk flags eight highs against axios 1.19.0 and fails the Analysis job on
every pull request: SSRF, ReDoS, prototype pollution, two confused-deputy
issues, two input-validation issues, and an unbounded allocation. All eight
are fixed in 1.20.0.

Nothing in flight introduced this. The advisories were published against a
version that has been in the lockfile since July, and it surfaced now only
because this is the first recent PR where the Analysis job ran rather than
being skipped.

The manifest range already permitted 1.20.0, so the floor moves with it to
stop a fresh install resolving back down. Axios's own dependency ranges are
unchanged, so nothing transitive moved.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#423

Six characterization tests cover reset / date-validation / invalid-date bail / success-merge / 404 paths. * refactor(EditSystemModal): extract reactivate flow into useReactivateFlow hook Three useStates + the handleReactivate body move into one hook with the same shape as useDecommissionFlow: notes / showForm / openAlert plus resetReactivateForm() and handleReactivate(system, onClose). Four characterization tests cover reset / success-merge / empty-body / 404 paths. EditSystemModal.tsx: 1245 -> 1001 LOC. * refactor(EditSystemModal): extract DecommissionedSystemInfo panel component Pull the read-only "decommissioned" details panel (date / by / notes / previous-reactivation line + the two action buttons) out into its own component. The parent passes pre-fill callbacks for the Edit Decommission Details and Reactivate buttons so the hook-owned form state stays in the orchestrator. EditSystemModal.tsx: 1001 -> 921 LOC. (The remaining DecommissionForm / ReactivateForm / SystemFormFields component splits are deferred - they're more entangled with the form-field validation handlers and worth a separate ticket.) * fix(UserTable): hide Delete button for the actor's own row (self-delete guard) UserTable shipped without a self-delete guard on the actions column - the Delete icon rendered for every in-tier active row, including the actor's own row. (Pre-existing on main, not introduced here, but still a bug.) Add an isSelf prop to ActionsCell that hides the Delete button when the row.userid matches userInfo.userid. Belt-and-braces: handleDeleteClick and handleConfirmDelete both short-circuit when target.userid is the actor's id, so a stale apiRef call cannot bypass the UI hide. The backend's own CanManageUser check already rejects self-delete; this makes the UI match. Add a characterization test pinning the guard. * fix(UserTable): match bugfix/638b0d6 - disable + tooltip Delete, don't hide Replace the previous "hide the Delete button" approach with the pattern shipped on the pre-redesign bugfix branch (commit 638b0d6 by the same author): keep the icon visible so the affordance is discoverable, but mark it disabled, swap the tooltip to "You can't delete your own account", and gray the icon. Hiding the button entirely left no signal that delete was a thing for that column. Also move the parent backstop into handleConfirmDelete (the bugfix's shape) and surface an explicit notify() instead of a silent return, so a programmatic invocation tells the user why nothing happened. Update the ActionsCell characterization test for the new pattern and switch all action-cell queries to getByRole so the MUI Tooltip's aria-label cloning onto the wrapper span doesn't collide with the button's own aria-label. * refactor(EditSystemModal): extract DecommissionForm + ReactivateForm sub-forms The DecommissionForm sub-form was duplicated inline in two places (the "Edit Decommission Details" affordance and the "Decommission System" toggle for an active system), differing only in indent, button label / color, and whether Cancel renders. Collapse both into one component with those four differences threaded as props. ReactivateForm lifts the single inline reactivate sub-form out by the same pattern. EditSystemModal.tsx: 921 -> 705 LOC. * refactor(EditSystemModal): extract SystemFormFields - two-column input grid Lift the ~300 LOC two-column form (Fisma Name/Acronym/UID + Component + Group/Division/Subsystem + Data Call Contact / ISSO Email + Datacenter Environment + SDL sync toggle) into SystemFormFields. The decommission/reactivate panel needs to render inside the right column (visually below the SDL sync toggle in the same grid item), so SystemFormFields accepts a children prop that renders at the bottom of the right column. The orchestrator passes the panel through that slot so the column layout stays exactly where it was - zero visual change. EditSystemModal.tsx: 705 -> 399 LOC. * test(EditSystemModal): add component-level characterization suite Six tests covering: loading guard (open w/o system renders nothing), initial render of edit mode with prepopulated values, Save changes -> PUT + success notify + onClose, decommissioned-system panel rendering with Edit/Reactivate buttons, opening the reactivate sub-form, and opening the decommission sub-form from the toggle for an active system. Closes the testing gap on #5 (EditSystemModal had no tests pre-refactor). * feat(questionnaire): require notes update when the answer changes When the user changes the radio answer, the save is blocked until the notes are substantially updated (trim-comparison — a trailing space does not count, matching the ticket's bonus criterion). Notes-only edits are unaffected. Unanswered questions and read-only sessions never trigger the rule. * New saveGuard helpers: `isSubstantialNotesChange` and `needsNotesUpdateForChoiceChange`. * Notes `CssTextField` gets error + `helperText` when the rule fires. * Next button disabled while the rule is unresolved. * `saveResponse()` has a defense-in-depth backstop for future save triggers. * a11y(508): contrast, labels, roles, and heading fixes across the redesign Contrast (WCAG 1.4.3 / 1.4.11, measured): - colors.border darkened #C7CCD6 -> #848D9C: input boundaries now clear the 3:1 bar on white (3.35) and neutral50 (3.15). Applied through the MuiOutlinedInput theme override (was 12%-alpha divider), fieldInputSx, and the remaining neutral200 fieldset/search-box borders. - ScoreDisplay not-assessed text and the unchecked radio/progress icons move neutral400 (2.54:1) -> neutral500 (5.97:1). - DecommissionForm/ReactivateForm native inputs drop the raw #ccc / #d32f2f for colors.border / colors.danger. Tier dots that miss 3:1 (Advanced, Not Assessed) stay as-is: each sits next to its tier name in text, so the color is redundant, not the sole carrier (1.4.11 exemption). Labels and associations (1.3.1 / 3.3.2 / 4.1.2): - Field error text gains role="alert" + a stable ${id}-error id; helper text gains ${id}-helper. - Modal wires aria-labelledby to its title (now an h2). - MUI Selects (OpDiv, datacenter environment) get labelId to the Field label; DecommissionForm/ReactivateForm date + notes inputs get real label htmlFor wiring and aria-invalid/aria-describedby on error; the questionnaire evidence textarea is now labeled by its visible text. Roles and announcements (4.1.2 / 4.1.3): - OptionCardList wraps its role=radio cards in role=radiogroup with an accessible name; OpDivGrantModal PillTab toggles carry aria-pressed. - SaveIndicator becomes an aria-live=polite region. - TrendRadar's role=img now has an aria-label pointing at the text equivalent in the pillar grid; initials avatars are aria-hidden since the adjacent name text carries the content. Structure (1.3.1): - Detail/pillar/insights card titles render as h2 under the PageHeader h1 so every page exposes a navigable heading outline. * test(EditSystemModal): pin Extended Metadata gating on extendedEditable Renders for organization-wide admins on create, absent for scoped tiers. Guards the Title.tsx -> hasUnscopedRead(userInfo) wiring from silently breaking in a future refactor. * fix(Home): pass extendedEditable to the Dashboard's Add-system modal The redesign moved Add System from the Title kebab into the Dashboard page header, giving Home.tsx its own EditSystemModal instance. The main merge wired extendedEditable={hasUnscopedRead(userInfo)} onto Title's instance only - the one the kebab opens - so the Dashboard button opened the modal without the Extended Metadata section even for OWNER/HHS-tier admins. Wire the same gate on Home's instance. * fix(AISummaryBadge): restyle with tokens so the app Chip theme can't crush it The badge arrived from main as a raw MUI Chip (color=info, outlined, height 18). The redesign theme sizes Chips for list contexts - forced 28px+ heights and icon margins tuned for 36px chips - which crushed the badge into a cramped artifact, and the template info palette rendered as translucent cyan with sub-AA contrast on white. Rebuild it as a token pill (primary50 / ink900, pill radius, 12px icon) in the StatusChip family. Also make it keyboard-focusable so the verify-before-signing-off tooltip is reachable without a mouse (508). Same show-prop contract for both consumers (questionnaire notes row, ScoreDiffModal). * fix(datacall-picker): year-grouped options and honest aggregate state The merge brought in main's year-grouped multi-call model but left the redesign picker rendering a flat list that displayed the first call as selected while the dashboard was actually aggregating the whole year. - Group options by fiscal year with CMS/HHS tenant labels. - Show an aggregate summary ("FY2026 - 3 calls"), the opens/closes range across the aggregated calls, and "In view" chips in the dropdown. - Allow clearing a single-call pick to return to the aggregated view. * fix(questionnaire): judge a picked call by its own deadline, not by rank A non-latest selected call was hardcoded as past-deadline, so picking a second concurrently-open call (e.g. FY27 Q3 while another call ranks as latest) showed the "datacall has closed" banner and went read-only for non-admins. Two calls can be open at once; read-only now follows the picked call's own deadline, matching the route-state and deep-link paths. * fix(datacalls): deadline order and per-call export target after the merge Main's #393/#549 rule - datacall recency is deadline order, not raw datacallid - was applied to main's own components but three redesign surfaces still ranked by id: the Home Avg ZT trend's prior call, the PillarScoresPage previous-call fallback, and the SystemDetailPage score hero. All three now index-walk the deadline-sorted scored-call list. Also ports main's export guard into Home's Export CSV: the target call derives from the selection's own call(s) via systemCallMap, and a selection spanning more than one call disables the button instead of silently exporting the latest call only. * a11y(508): keyboard and screen-reader fixes across merged surfaces - Account avatar is a real button (was a role="button" Box with no tabIndex or key handler - the only path to Log out was mouse-only). - Add a skip-to-main-content link; programmatic focus because hash routing swallows in-page fragment anchors. - Restore the questionnaire question's heading semantics (h2 under the PageHeader h1), lost when the redesign card replaced main's layout. - Progress column states are focusable with complete accessible names; tooltips open on keyboard focus, and the no-data dash carries visually-hidden text instead of an aria-label on a plain span. * feat(datacall): enhance DatacallContextCard with viewedDatacall and onPick props for improved call handling * fix(validators): accept the full local-part charset the backend stores The email regex rejected '+' and other RFC local-part characters that the backend (mail.ParseAddress) accepts, so an already-stored address could fail validation on load and freeze the edit form. * fix(dashboard): restore the multi-select data-call picker (#467) The redesign's context card was single-select only, so aggregate views of non-latest years and per-call subsets were unreachable. The pill now opens a year-grouped menu of checkbox rows with main's toggle rules: a call in another year selects that whole year, in-year clicks toggle without emptying the year, and the menu stays open across toggles. The clear X still resets to the latest year; the questionnaire's picker stays single-pick. * fix(dashboard): one-click Clear filters and stronger past-call muting Clear filters resets search, Environment, OpDiv, both call-scoped toggles, and Show Decommissioned at once (#566/#573 parity); enabled only while something is active. Past-call rows now mute their plain-text columns per-field on top of the background tint, while links, chips, and scores keep full contrast. * feat(dashboard): restore Highest/Lowest score tiles named by acronym Re-adds the best/worst system callouts the redesign's stat row dropped, with '-' placeholders when nothing is scored, and restores the average-between-bounds regression test (#633). * feat(questionnaire): show per-pillar 'N to confirm' counts in the rail The split rails left carried-forward confirmation markers visible only for the current section. Each pillar row now carries a text-bearing count from the same carryForwardState classification the section rail and Complete summary use. * refactor(system-detail): restyle the delegates section onto ui primitives Swaps the stock MUI Card/Chip/Dialog shell for the redesign card, StatusChip badges, and the shared Modal + Field forms. Behavior, labels, and aria names unchanged; all 15 section tests pass untouched. * fix(ui): document scroll with fixed-height grids (parity with main) Reverts the fixed-viewport app-shell: `#root` uses `min-height` and the page scrolls, pushing the CMS footer down. The Dashboard / Users / OpDivs grids get main's fixed 600px box and scroll their rows internally, so a useful number of rows is always visible regardless of viewport height. * fix(dashboard): tighter score column, wider Data Call, no Status column Stack the tier word above the score bar (ScoreDisplay stacked mode) and hand the freed width to the Data Call column, whose names were truncating. Drop the Status column: the decommissioned toggle swaps the fetch, so a view is always all-active or all-decommissioned and the column could never differ within one. * fix(questionnaire): name the last editor on the save indicator The save indicator received the response's last_edited_by data but only revealed it on hover, so the footer read "Saved " with no author. The pre-redesign footer named the editor inline, so the change was lost on screen once the questionnaire moved to the indicator. Append "by " to the visible line when the server reports an editor, and keep the full role, email, and exact time in the hover tooltip. * fix(questionnaire): drop the no-op "Submit responses" button Every answer persists on its own when the user clicks Next or Complete; there is no submit endpoint. The button only toasted a save count and navigated to the system detail page, which the System Info button already does, so it implied a finalize step that does not exist and duplicated existing navigation. Leaving the questionnaire is now System Info or the breadcrumb. * fix(theme): stop link-styled buttons showing the visited color A `Button` rendered as a router link is a real anchor, so the browser repainted its label with the visited color and made it look like a followed link. Pin the visited color to each primary variant's resting color in the `MuiButton` theme override, so any current or future link-button keeps its normal appearance. * fix(events): align the audit table with the redesign table conventions * fix(events): themed date pickers, clear-filters, and readable labels Swap the audit filter's native date inputs for MUI DatePickers so the field and calendar inherit the design tokens (adds @mui/x-date-pickers, on the already-present date-fns v3). Add a Clear filters action that resets every filter and returns to the first page. Render the Action and Resource columns as human-readable labels ("Created", "System assignment") instead of raw verbs and database table names, with a prettified fallback for unmapped values. Also lands the dateBounds helper the pickers depend on, which the previous commit imported but left untracked. * fix(buttons): ensure link-styled buttons maintain color consistency for visited states * feat(questionnaire): promote progress to a full-width bar under the header Replace the compact SubtitleLine text ("42 of 147 questions answered · last saved 2 min ago") with QuestionnaireProgress, a full-width LinearProgress row placed below the page header. Completion now reads at a glance via bar fill plus a floored percentage, with the answered/total count carried in the bar's accessible name for screen readers. Percentage is floored (never rounded) so 100% is reserved for genuine completion - 99.5% still reads 99%. Before questions load, a height-reserving skeleton prevents the datacall card below from jumping. Save timing no longer lives here; the footer SaveIndicator already owns that. Update the loading-state test to account for the bar being a persistent element (not just a transient loading spinner) * fix(a11y): label pagination and focus grid scrollers * refactor(dashboard): simplify systems table * refactor(dashboard): rebalance toolbar controls * fix(ui): adjust search input width for better usability * refactor(dashboard): order toolbar switches first * refactor(system-detail): pair metadata and maturity cards * style: unify system detail cards * test: stabilize questionnaire loading gate * fix(questionnaire): count only confirmed, in-scope answers toward completion Two ways progress numbers could overstate completion: * **Carried-forward answer counts:** Carried-forward answers counted as complete as soon as their score rows existed, showing questions as answered on open calls before user confirmation or editing. `isQuestionComplete` now excludes unconfirmed carried-forward rows on open calls; closed calls and pre-status API responses retain row-presence logic. * **Out-of-scope score rows:** Answered totals derived directly from raw score-row counts, which included functions rendered inapplicable by environment or scope changes. This allowed the numerator to exceed the total (for example, "42 of 40"). The calculation now sums the same category steps used to calculate total questions, preventing the count from exceeding the denominator. * test(DatacallContextCardView): Fix datacall component date tense handling + tests * feat(navigation): Address pillar score questionnare navigation feedback and unify system workflow header actions * fix(pillar-scores): keep datacall comparisons isolated to modal *  fix(score-comparison): widen modal to prevent table clipping * feat(FismaTable): enhance toolbar and environment filter options layout * feat(FismaTable): add tooltips for system identity, data center, and FIPS columns * feat(UserTable, ActionsCell): center align action buttons for improved UI consistency * fix(tables,pillar-scores): page off server totals and resolve systems by id The shared `DataGrid` footer derived its page count from `gridPageCountSelector`, which evaluates only loaded rows. In server-paginated mode this evaluates to a single page, causing the Events audit log to render a single disabled page control and hiding 203 of 253 records. The count now derives from the `rowCount` prop when a server total is provided, while client-paginated tables retain the filtered row count selector. The Pillar Scores view resolved system contexts strictly from active-system lists, causing decommissioned or unlisted system IDs to render blank screens instead of resolving system details by ID. System resolution now queries directly by system ID with active-list lookups retained as a fallback. * feat(refactor): Update comments and test descriptions to use consistent punctuation style * feat(dates): implement formatDate and formatDateTime utilities for consistent date formatting across components
